## Overview

scMetaIntegrator (scMI) tests for differential expression in paired single-cell RNA-seq data. Each matched pair, such as one donor measured under two conditions, is treated as one study. Within a pair, scMI compares cells from the two conditions and computes a per-gene effect size (Hedges' g). It then pools the effect sizes across pairs with random-effects meta-analysis using [MetaIntegrator](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=MetaIntegrator).

This article walks through a complete analysis on simulated data, from checking the pairing to plotting the results. Loading the MetaIntegrator package is required to run scMetaIntegrator.

| Step | Function | What it does |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Validate | `confirmPairs()` | Checks that every pair has exactly two samples |
| Subset | `completePairSubset()` | Keeps only complete pairs |
| Filter genes | `thresholdGenesAcrossPairs()` | Keeps genes expressed in a minimum fraction of cells in every pair |
| Run (simple output) | `runscMI()` | Returns one table of pooled results per gene |
| Run (full object) | `generateFullMA()` | Returns a MetaIntegrator `metaObject` for forest plots, gene scores and leave-one-out filtering |

```{r library}
library(scMetaIntegrator)
library(Seurat)
library(MetaIntegrator)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## Data requirements

scMI needs a Seurat v5 object with log-normalized expression in the `data` layer and three metadata columns.

| Metadata column | What it holds | Example in this article |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Unique sample ID | One value per sample | `sample` (`donor1_CTRL`) |
| Pairing variable | The value shared by the two samples in a pair | `donor` (`donor1`) |
| Comparison variable | The two conditions to compare | `condition` (`STIM`, `CTRL`) |

Every pair must contain exactly two samples, one per condition.

## 1. Simulate a paired scRNA-seq experiment

We simulate four donors, each sampled under a control and a stimulated condition, with 80 cells per sample. Three genes (`GENE1` to `GENE3`) are up-regulated in the stimulated condition.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(4)
n_genes   = 300
genes     = paste0("GENE", seq_len(n_genes))
donors    = paste0("donor", 1:4)
conds     = c("CTRL", "STIM")
n_cells   = 80
de_genes  = c("GENE1", "GENE2", "GENE3")
base_mean = rgamma(n_genes, shape = 1, rate = 1)
names(base_mean) = genes

counts_list = list()
meta_list   = list()
for (d in donors) {
  for (cnd in conds) {
    mu = base_mean
    if (cnd == "STIM") mu[de_genes] = mu[de_genes] * 3
    size_factor = rlnorm(n_cells, 0, 0.2)
    m = sapply(size_factor, function(sf) rnbinom(n_genes, mu = mu * sf, size = 2))
    sample_id = paste(d, cnd, sep = "_")
    cell_ids  = paste(sample_id, seq_len(n_cells), sep = "_")
    dimnames(m) = list(genes, cell_ids)
    counts_list[[sample_id]] = m
    meta_list[[sample_id]] = data.frame(sample    = rep(sample_id, n_cells),
                                        donor     = rep(d, n_cells),
                                        condition = rep(cnd, n_cells),
                                        row.names = cell_ids)
  }
}

seu = CreateSeuratObject(counts = do.call(cbind, counts_list),
                         meta.data = do.call(rbind, meta_list))
seu = NormalizeData(seu)
table(seu$donor, seu$condition)
```

## 2. Check the pairing

```{r confirm}
confirmPairs(seu, uniqueSampleID = "sample", pairingColumn = "donor")
```

`TRUE` means every donor has exactly two samples. If it returns `FALSE`, drop the incomplete pairs with `completePairSubset()`, or set `completePairsOnly = TRUE` in `runscMI()` or `generateFullMA()`.

```{r complete}
seu = completePairSubset(seu, uniqueSampleID = "sample", pairingColumn = "donor")
```

## 3. Choose genes to test

`thresholdGenesAcrossPairs()` keeps genes detected in at least `percentThreshold` of cells in every pair. Passing the result as `thresholdGenes` restricts the analysis to those genes and reduces memory use.

```{r threshold}
thresholdedGenes = thresholdGenesAcrossPairs(
  seuratObject     = seu,
  uniqueSampleID   = "sample",
  pairingColumn    = "donor",
  percentThreshold = 0.01
)
length(thresholdedGenes)
```

## 4. Run scMI

`groupOne` is the condition whose effect you want to estimate. `groupTwo` is the reference, usually the control. A positive effect size means higher expression in `groupOne`.

```{r runscMI}
scMI_output = runscMI(
  seuratObject          = seu,
  uniqueSampleID        = "sample",
  pairingColumn         = "donor",
  comparisonGroupColumn = "condition",
  groupOne              = "STIM",
  groupTwo              = "CTRL",
  thresholdGenes        = thresholdedGenes
)
head(scMI_output[order(scMI_output$effectSizeFDR), ])
```

The columns are the pooled effect size (`effectSize`), its p-value and FDR (`effectSizePval`, `effectSizeFDR`), a Bonferroni-adjusted p-value (`effectSizeBF`), and the number of pairs that contributed (`numPairs`).

The three genes we up-regulated in the simulation should show positive effect sizes.

```{r planted}
scMI_output[scMI_output$gene %in% de_genes, ]
```

### Count differentially expressed genes

```{r nsig}
table(Significant = scMI_output$effectSizeFDR < 0.05,
      Direction   = ifelse(scMI_output$effectSize > 0, "positive", "negative"))
```

### Volcano plot

Genes with an FDR below 0.05 and an absolute effect size above 0.5 are colored and labeled. FDR values of 0 are set to 1e-300 so they can be plotted on a log scale.

```{r volcano, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5.5}
volcano_df = scMI_output
volcano_df$neg_log10_fdr = -log10(pmax(volcano_df$effectSizeFDR, 1e-300))
volcano_df$category = ifelse(volcano_df$effectSizeFDR < 0.05 & volcano_df$effectSize >  0.5, "Up in STIM",
                      ifelse(volcano_df$effectSizeFDR < 0.05 & volcano_df$effectSize < -0.5, "Up in CTRL",
                             "Not significant"))
volcano_df$category = factor(volcano_df$category,
                             levels = c("Up in STIM", "Up in CTRL", "Not significant"))

label_df = volcano_df[volcano_df$category != "Not significant", ]

ggplot(volcano_df, aes(x = effectSize, y = neg_log10_fdr, color = category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-0.5, 0.5), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_text_repel(data = label_df, aes(label = gene), color = "black", size = 3.5,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.5, segment.color = "grey60") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Up in STIM"      = "#A40000FF",
                                "Up in CTRL"      = "#16317DFF",
                                "Not significant" = "grey70")) +
  labs(x = "Pooled effect size (Hedges' g)",
       y = expression(-log[10](FDR)),
       color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 5. Get the full MetaIntegrator object

`generateFullMA()` returns the full MetaIntegrator object. The pooled table is in `$metaAnalysis$pooledResults` and contains extra columns such as `tauSquared` for between-pair heterogeneity. Here we set `runLeaveOneOut = TRUE` because section 7 filters genes with leave-one-out support, and `maxCores = 2` to limit the number of parallel processes.

```{r fullMA}
scMIObj = generateFullMA(
  seuratObject          = seu,
  uniqueSampleID        = "sample",
  pairingColumn         = "donor",
  comparisonGroupColumn = "condition",
  groupOne              = "STIM",
  groupTwo              = "CTRL",
  thresholdGenes        = thresholdedGenes,
  maxCores              = 2,
  runLeaveOneOut        = TRUE
)
pooled_res = scMIObj$metaAnalysis$pooledResults
head(pooled_res[order(pooled_res$effectSizeFDR), c("gene", "effectSize", "effectSizeFDR", "tauSquared", "numPairs")])
```

### Forest plot for one gene

A forest plot shows the per-pair effect sizes and the pooled estimate.

```{r forest}
forestPlot(scMIObj, "GENE1")
```

## 6. Memory and speed options

Both functions share three arguments that control memory use.

| Argument | Default in `generateFullMA()` | Default in `runscMI()` | Effect |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `runLeaveOneOut` | `FALSE` | `FALSE` | Runs k extra meta-analyses, each leaving out one pair. Required by `MetaIntegrator::filterGenes(isLeaveOneOut = TRUE)`. Pooled results are identical either way |
| `keepExpr` | `TRUE` | `FALSE` | Keeps the per-pair expression matrices in the returned object. Required for `forestPlot()`, `calculateScore()` and `pooledROCPlot()` |
| `maxCores` | `NULL` | `NULL` | Number of cores passed to `MetaIntegrator::runMetaAnalysis()` |

For large objects, filter genes with `thresholdGenes`, and use `runscMI()` when only the pooled table is needed.

## 7. Filter genes with leave-one-out support

When the full object was built with `runLeaveOneOut = TRUE` (as in section 5), MetaIntegrator can filter to genes whose significance holds when any single pair is removed.

```{r filter}
scMIObj = filterGenes(scMIObj, isLeaveOneOut = TRUE, FDRThresh = 0.05)
names(scMIObj$filterResults)
```
